distinguishing_features: A physical metal-to-metal lip seal replaces the elastomeric O-ring instead of merely monitoring seal condition.
Contact pressure is generated by CTE mismatch between a higher-expansion metallic lip and a lower-expansion body sleeve.
The steel/316L lip and Invar 36 body pair is selected to create thermal interference/contact stress above hydraulic pressure.
Validation is by measured leak-rate reduction under combined pressure and thermal cycling rather than temperature/pressure signal divergence.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Maintaining seal-face contact and preventing leakage in a subsea hydraulic connector subjected to pressure and thermal cycling despite relaxation or degradation of conventional elastomer seals.
parsed.viable_reason: As written it assumes an unsupported sustained 50 K lip-to-body differential and does not define the constrained geometry or preload needed to convert CTE mismatch into seal-face contact pressure, so the claimed 105 MPa contact pressure is not established.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Prior art 1 only infers seal or flush distress from temperature-pressure divergence and does not teach or suggest a CTE-mismatched metal lip/body structure that self-energizes the seal.
